column1: HOW TO ADD OR CHANGE ITEMS IN THE MVP PRICE LIST AND CHECK-UP

The price list has one tab per trade: Electrical, HVAC, Plumbing. The check-up list (what techs check and what customers read) has three more tabs: Check-up Electrical, Check-up HVAC, Check-up Plumbing. The app reads all of them about every 10 minutes and checks them before using them. This tab is only instructions — the app ignores it.

column2: Open the tab for the trade (Electrical, HVAC or Plumbing) and add a new row at the bottom.
Fill in every column (see the table below). Don't leave a price empty.
Wait up to 10 minutes, or in the app go to Office → Prices & check-up → Sync now.
Check the message in Office → Prices & check-up: ✓ means it's live. A red box says which tab and row to fix — until then the app keeps the old prices.
WHAT TO PUT
A new code nobody else uses. Electrical tab: EL-…, HVAC tab: HV-…, Plumbing tab: PL-…, then a number.
The same as the tab: Electrical, HVAC or Plumbing.
A group name. Techs see items grouped by it (Panel, Drains, Motors, Replacement…).
What the job is, in plain words. Customers see this on estimates.
Estimated hours (for reference only).
Price for non-members. Numbers only — no $ needed.
Price for members. Can't be higher than standard_price. Put 0 if the membership includes it.
Service = repairs and small jobs. Install = replacements and new installs.
Leave EMPTY for repairs. For replacements: Small ($100), Medium ($250) or Large ($500) member credit.
Optional. Internal note shown to techs.
Just edit the number in the cell. Reports and estimates already sent to customers keep the old price.
Delete its row. The app won't allow removing an item that the check-up guide or the service call still uses — it will say which one.
Don't change, move or rename the first row of each trade tab (the column names).
Don't delete or rename the Electrical, HVAC and Plumbing tabs. If you ever re-link the sheet in the app, copy each tab's link while that tab is open.
Each code only once, across all three tabs. Don't reuse a code from a deleted item for something different.
EL-100, HV-100 and PL-100 are the service calls ($19 members / $119 non-members). Don't delete them.
Service calls: the $119 is never credited toward the repair. Joining the club is the only way to get $19.
Right away — techs find it under “+ Add items from the price book”.
Only when a check-up finding points to its code (pricebook_code column on a Check-up tab — see below).

column1: CHECK-UP TABS (Check-up Electrical, Check-up HVAC, Check-up Plumbing)

column2: Each row is one possible finding: what the tech checks, what they might find, how urgent it is, the fix from the price list, and the words the customer reads on the report.
Rows are shown to techs in the same order as the tab. Rows with the same area are grouped together.
Add a row on the right Check-up tab, fill every column, then wait 10 minutes or press Sync now. Same ✓ / red box message as prices.
Edit the cell. Check-ups already sent to customers keep the old wording.
Delete its row. Old check-ups that used it are not affected.
WHAT TO PUT
A new id nobody else uses. Check-up Electrical: EI-…, Check-up HVAC: HI-…, Check-up Plumbing: PI-…, then a number.
The same as the tab: Electrical, HVAC or Plumbing.
The part of the house or system. Techs see findings grouped by it.
What the tech does to check it. Put "Same" to repeat the row above in the same area.

A code from the price list tabs (the customer sees that price), or Quote (the office prepares a price), or EMPTY for GREEN rows with nothing to sell.
The headline the customer reads on the report.

column2: Any trained tech, or Trade tech (only the licensed trade partner).
Prices are NOT typed on the Check-up tabs — they always come from the price list tabs through pricebook_code.
A pricebook_code must exist in the price list. To use a new item, add it on the price tab first (the app accepts both changes in the same sync).
Don't change the first row of the Check-up tabs (the column names) or rename the tabs.
Editors: owner and office. Trades: Viewer or Commenter (they see prices and suggest changes with comments).
Every change the app publishes is listed in Office → Prices & check-up → History (what changed, when, by whom).
